Definition: from G3173; greatness, i.e. (figuratively) divinity (often God himself):--majesty.
BiblicalUsage: Majesty is the greatness of God Himself, and Hebrews uses it for the place of Christ: He sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high, and we have a high priest set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens. Jude closes his letter with glory and majesty to the only wise God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Majesty on high is the throne Christ sits on: He purged our sins and sat down, because the work was finished, and the high priest who sits is the proof that the way to God is open. I hold that majesty is not distance but the glory of a Saviour who reigns.
